correctness.rationale: For the alternating central bracket [e1,e2,e3]=e4, substituting block T=(A,u;v,t) into the exact nonabelian identity gives a U-component forcing u=0: if u were nonzero, varying e4 coordinates would force im A⊂Ku, then the remaining ω(x,y,z) term could not vanish. With u=0 the scalar condition on all x,y,z is t(adj(A)+I3)=det(A)I3. If t=0, all singular A work with arbitrary v. If t≠0, adj(A) must be nonzero scalar and invertible, hence A=λI3 with λ≠0 and t(λ²+1)=λ³; the scalar branch is disjoint. The finite field count q³(singular 3×3 matrices + permissible λ) and rank profile follow by whether covector v lies in row space(A). Independently enumerated all 65,536 linear maps over F2 and checked original ternary polynomial identity on all basis triples: 2,752 solutions, rank counts (1,105,1470,1176,0), matching formula. Characteristic zero checks show the v1 diag(1,1,2k,k) example is valid only k=0,1/2, not generic. Arbitrary-field theorem follows from adjugate proof, not finite enumeration.

The singular-matrix family plus separate invertible scalar curve, with free v and finite-field rank strata, vastly extends a single published example. This remains valuable independently of the prior correction of the flawed earlier example. It does not purport to classify arbitrary 3-Lie algebras or quotient by automorphisms.
